sections.html:
Webster County is in central Iowa, and its county seat and largest city is Fort Dodge. It covers 718 square miles, of which 716 are land, and was created on January 15, 1851 as one of 43 counties established in a single act. The county is named for Daniel Webster.

Pocahontas and Humboldt counties lie to the north, Wright to the northeast, Hamilton to the east, Boone to the southeast, Greene to the southwest and Calhoun to the west.

sections.h2: How many people live in Webster County?
sections.html:
Webster County had 36,999 residents in the 2020 census and an estimated 36,838 in 2025. The county peaked at 48,391 people in 1970 and has lost population since.

Roughly two thirds of residents live in urban areas, and the median age is 40.2.

sections.h2: What does the Census Bureau show for Webster County housing?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau reports a median value of $153,800 for owner-occupied homes in Webster County for 2020 to 2024, and 70.3 percent of homes are owner-occupied. The county had an estimated 17,209 housing units on July 1, 2025.

  • Median gross rent: $785
  • Median household income: $68,975
  • Persons per household: 2.21
  • Bachelor's degree or higher, age 25+: 22.0%
  • Mean travel time to work: 20.2 minutes

These are county medians. A Fort Dodge house, a farm dwelling near Gowrie and a small town house in Lehigh can differ widely in value.

Fort Dodge began as an army post. On August 2, 1850, Captain Samuel Woods and Company E of the 6th Infantry arrived to build a fort where Lizard Creek meets the Des Moines River.

The post was first called Fort Clarke and then renamed for Henry Dodge, a former governor of Wisconsin Territory. The army left in 1853, a storekeeper named William Williams bought the land and buildings the next year, and the town was incorporated in 1869.

In 1872 the Fort Dodge Plaster Mills opened a gypsum mill, described as the first west of the Mississippi River. Gypsum from the area was used for the Cardiff Giant hoax, and a replica is on display at the Fort Museum and Frontier Village.

sections.h2: What drives the Webster County economy?
sections.html:
Fort Dodge has a mix of processing and manufacturing: biofuels, livestock feed, gypsum and limestone mining, can production, drywall, trucking and veterinary pharmaceuticals. National Gypsum, Georgia Pacific, CertainTeed and United States Gypsum have plants in or near the city.

  • Elanco, which makes animal health products, has two of its three U.S. manufacturing plants in Fort Dodge.
  • Cargill announced a corn syrup refinery in 2022.
  • The Fort Dodge Correctional Facility, a 1,250-bed medium security prison, opened in 1998.
  • UnityPoint Hospital, formerly Trinity Regional Medical Center, is the city's only hospital.

Meatpacking was a leading industry for most of the 20th century, and the last two large plants, owned by Iowa Beef Processors and Hormel, closed in the 1980s. Iowa Central Community College has its central campus in Fort Dodge.

sections.h2: What is the climate in Fort Dodge, and what does it mean for a house?
sections.html:
Fort Dodge has a humid continental climate with cold winters and hot, humid summers. NOAA normals for 1991 to 2020 give an annual mean high of 56.9 degrees F and an annual mean low of 36.0 degrees F.

Average precipitation is 35.09 inches a year and average snowfall is 39.0 inches. The record low is minus 35 degrees F and the record high is 110 degrees F.

A house here has to cope with deep winter cold, snow and humid summer heat, which is worth keeping in mind when a seller weighs repairs against selling as-is.

sections.h2: How do roads, schools and transit work in Webster County?
sections.html:
US 20 crosses the middle of the county and bypasses Fort Dodge to the south, while US 169 passes on the west side and runs south to Harcourt. Iowa 7 ends at the northwest edge of the city, and Iowa 175 and Iowa 144 serve the southeast and south.

Fort Dodge Regional Airport, just north of the city, is mainly a general aviation field with daily flights to St. Louis and Minneapolis-St. Paul. DART runs six local bus routes on weekdays.

School districts in the county include Fort Dodge, Webster City, Eagle Grove, Gilmore City-Bradgate, Humboldt, Manson Northwest Webster, Stratford and Southeast Valley, which formed in 2023 from a merger.

sections.h2: Which Webster County offices handle property tax?
sections.html:
The treasurer, assessor, recorder and auditor are all at the Webster County Courthouse, 701 Central Avenue, Fort Dodge. Hours are Monday through Friday, generally 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

  • Treasurer: 515-576-4611. Taxes can be paid online through iowatreasurers.org.
  • Assessor: 515-576-4721, assessor@webstercountyia.gov. Property records are on the county's Beacon site.
  • Recorder: 515-576-2401. The recording cutoff for real estate is 3:00 p.m. The office also collects transfer tax for the Iowa Department of Revenue.
  • Auditor: 515-573-7175. This office prepares and certifies tax levies and keeps real estate transfer records.

sections.h2: How does the Webster County assessment and appeal calendar work?
sections.html:
Webster County revalues real property every two years, in odd-numbered years, with an effective date of January 1. Market value is an estimate of what the property would sell for on that date.

For 2026, assessment notices were expected around March 20. Informal meetings with Vanguard Appraisals began April 2, with appointments requested by April 17 at 515-576-4721, and written Board of Review protests were accepted April 2 through April 30. The Board has three or five members and can raise or lower a value.

A decision can be appealed to the Property Assessment Appeal Board or the district court within 20 days after the Board adjourns, or by May 31, whichever is later.

The county also ran a reappraisal of agricultural dwellings and rural residential property from 2024 to 2026. New values take effect January 1, 2026, for taxes payable in fiscal 2027 and 2028.

sections.h2: What are the county levy rates and new taxes?
sections.html:
For fiscal 2025 to 2026, Webster County's levy was $7.12 per $1,000 of taxable value for urban property, including Fort Dodge, and $10.78 for rural property. The county's tax asking was $19,578,775, up less than 1 percent.

The levy includes a new EMS tax of 75 cents per $1,000, which voters approved on March 4, 2025 by an 83 percent margin. It is expected to raise about $1.6 million a year.

Fort Dodge proposed a city levy of $20.75 per $1,000 for the year starting July 1, 2025. Its parts included $8.54 for the general fund, $6.54 for employee benefits and $4.50 for bond debt.

In March 2026 the county said residential rates fell 2.37 percent for urban property and 1.76 percent for rural. Commercial rates rose 4.97 percent and 5.62 percent. Some owners still saw higher bills because assessments went up.

sections.h2: When are Webster County taxes due, and what if they are not paid?
sections.html:
Iowa taxes are paid in two halves, due September 1 and March 1, with late interest of 1.5 percent a month starting October 1 and April 1. In a sale, taxes are usually prorated and the buyer is credited with the seller's share.

Unpaid taxes can go to tax sale. The owner can redeem by paying the sale amount plus 2 percent a month and fees of $20 each for the certificate and redemption, and a tax sale deed can follow if the redemption period passes.

Transfers carry a state transfer tax of 80 cents per $500 above the first $500, payable by the seller under Iowa Code 428A.3.

sections.h2: What should a Fort Dodge landlord know before selling?
sections.html:
Fort Dodge rental properties must be registered and inspected under Ordinance 2204 of the municipal code. An updated rental ordinance with a four-star rating system took effect October 1, 2022.

A unit rented without a valid certificate of rental housing compliance may be ordered vacated, and the owner may be cited. The city's Neighborhood Wellness Coordinator is at City Hall, 819 1st Avenue South, 515-576-4551 extension 1252. We buy Webster County houses as-is, including rentals that need work.

faqs.q: What is the county seat of Webster County, Iowa?
faqs.a: Fort Dodge is the county seat and largest city, with 24,871 residents in 2020. County offices are at the courthouse, 701 Central Avenue.

faqs.q: When can I protest a Webster County assessment?
faqs.a: File a written protest with the Board of Review between April 2 and April 30. The assessor's office, at 515-576-4721, handles the informal review step before that.

faqs.q: How much is the new Webster County EMS tax?
faqs.a: The EMS tax is 75 cents per $1,000 of taxable value. Voters approved it on March 4, 2025, and it is expected to raise about $1.6 million a year.

faqs.q: Does Webster County have a tax sale?
faqs.a: Yes. Unpaid property tax can be sold at tax sale, and the owner can redeem by paying the amount sold plus 2 percent per month and fees. Contact the treasurer at 515-576-4611 for a payoff.

faqs.q: Who pays Iowa transfer tax in Webster County?
faqs.a: The seller pays. The rate is 80 cents for each $500 above the first $500, and the recorder collects it before recording the deed.
